headline: Kai, America votes today: Congress is in play, traders put a Senate flip near 75%, and AMD reports after the close.
subline: Futures are split ahead of tonight's count, Apple's memory-cost warning weighs on tech, and oil is bouncing after Monday's 7% slide.
asof: Pre-market · futures and overnight quotes as of ~6:40 AM ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Markets brace for tonight's midterm count
items.sentence: Traders go into the results pricing a nearly 75% chance Democrats take the Senate, and JPMorgan warns a sweep of both chambers could trigger a sell-off in AI stocks, per Stocktwits, citing CNBC.

items.title: Apple drops 4.5% on memory-cost warning
items.sentence: Apple fell 4.5% premarket after saying surging memory-chip prices will keep pressuring gross margin, even though revenue and iPhone sales beat expectations, per Stocktwits.

items.title: Oil rebounds after Monday's 7% plunge
items.sentence: Brent settled 7.63% lower at $104.77 and WTI at $96.46 on US-Iran settlement hopes, then crude bounced more than 1% overnight on reports of a US strike on Qeshm Island, per ATFX and Stocktwits.

items.title: JOLTS and factory orders today; AMD tonight
items.sentence: September job openings (7.1 million expected) and factory orders land this morning, then AMD — with Q4 guidance the swing factor — leads an after-the-bell slate that includes Pfizer, Shopify and Super Micro, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Bitcoin defends $76,500 as ETF outflows run on
items.sentence: Spot bitcoin ETFs bled $398.6 million on November 2 after $643.3 million on October 30, stretching bitcoin's seven-day decline to 3.59% with support eyed at $76,400, per crypto.news.

items.title: Election Day: control of Congress on the line
items.sentence: Voting wraps up today in midterms that decide control of both the House and Senate, with CBS News tracking results live as polls close tonight.

items.title: Record spending, low approval frame the vote
items.sentence: Campaign spending is projected at $11.9 billion, the most expensive midterm on record, while Trump enters the day at 32% approval, just above his 31% low, per 10 Things News.

items.title: Russian strike kills 26 ahead of peace talks
items.sentence: Russian airstrikes on an aid centre and shelter in southern Ukraine killed at least 26 people a week before delegations meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, per 10 Things News.

items.title: US-Iran talks grind on without breakthrough
items.sentence: Indirect negotiations through Qatari mediators have produced revised proposals but no deal, and Tehran says its seven-step plan could be implemented within two days, per 10 Things News.

items.title: Cyberattacks hit supermarket freezers across Europe
items.sentence: Suspected cyberattacks altered refrigeration temperatures at supermarkets in seven European countries on Monday, forcing stores to discard food, per 10 Things News.

items.title: Palantir beats, raises outlook; stock drops 5%
items.sentence: Palantir beat Q3 estimates, raised its full-year revenue outlook, and saw US commercial sales pass government sales for the first time, but the stock fell about 5% premarket on valuation worries, per Yahoo Finance and Stocktwits.

items.title: Marvell strikes $115 billion deal for Lumentum
items.sentence: Marvell agreed to buy AI-optics maker Lumentum in a deal Stocktwits puts at $115 billion, and its shares rose more than 2% premarket on the news.

items.title: Oracle raises $20 billion; shares fall 8.6%
items.sentence: Oracle dropped 8.6% Monday after launching a roughly $20 billion equity-and-bond raise that prices 86.2 million shares at $116, well below the 50-day average of $141.25, per Stocktwits.

items.title: Four AI labs back one training opt-out
items.sentence: Google, OpenAI, Microsoft and Anthropic agreed to honor a single robots.txt opt-out token for AI training, with Microsoft committing from February 2027 and Google targeting early 2027, per The Next Web.

items.title: UK: AI-powered infrastructure attack likely by 2028
items.sentence: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre says an AI-powered ransomware attack on critical national infrastructure is highly likely by 2028, per 10 Things News.
